title: The Octopus: An Alien Mind
intro: 章魚有三顆心臟、藍色血液，還有一個分布全身的「大腦」。牠們有多聰明？
passage:
If you want to meet an intelligent alien, you do not need a spaceship. You need a [[1]] permit and a tide pool. The octopus, which last shared a common ancestor with humans more than 500 million years ago, has evolved a form of intelligence so [[2]] from ours that scientists describe it as the closest we can come to studying an alien mind.
The most obvious difference is architecture. In vertebrates, most thinking happens in the brain; in the octopus, roughly two thirds of its neurons are [[3]] through its eight arms. Each arm can taste, touch and make decisions [[4]], and a severed arm will still reach for food. This raises questions that keep philosophers busy: when an octopus's arms [[5]] problems, who exactly is solving them?
Laboratory studies hint at how much is going on inside. Octopuses learn to open childproof pill bottles, remember which of two mazes leads to food, and [[6]] the lights in their tanks by squirting water at bulbs — apparently for fun. At a New Zealand aquarium, an octopus named Inky became famous for [[7]]: he slipped out of a gap in his tank lid, crossed the floor at night, and escaped down a fifty-metre drainpipe to the sea.
Yet intelligence of this kind [[8]] a serious ethical question for zoos and researchers. Animals that solve puzzles also get bored, and boredom in a [[9]] animal looks like stress: ink clouds, lost arms, refusal to eat. Several European countries now require special licences to keep octopuses, and some aquariums are redesigning tanks to make them more [[10]].
Their short lives add a melancholy note. Most species live only one or two years, dying shortly after reproducing. Evolution, it seems, was [[11]] to spend resources on a big brain and a long childhood at the same time; nature chose the brain. Each animal must therefore [[12]] nearly everything alone, without parents or teachers — building its brilliant, temporary mind from [[13]].
That fact makes their achievements more [[14]], not less. A human child learns within a culture that stores knowledge across generations; an octopus starts from zero and still works out the world. Perhaps the surest sign of an [[15]] mind is not what it knows, but how much it can manage without ever being told.

questions.note: 接觸潮汐池裡的章魚需要「捕撈/垂釣」許可，fishing permit 呼應科學研究的場景；travelling、driving、trading 與潮池無關。
下文 closest we can come to studying an alien mind 點明章魚智力與人類「差異極大」；similar 與 alien mind 矛盾；inferior、superior 帶比較級含義但文中無高下之分。
三分之二的神經元「分布」在八條腕足中——呼應後文每條腕足能獨立決策；distributed 與下文獨立性一致；locked 與 make decisions 矛盾。
「各腕足能獨立」嚐味、觸碰並做決定，呼應 two thirds of neurons 分布於腕足；independently 為核心概念；reluctantly、occasionally 與下文 severed arm still reaches 矛盾。
腕足「解決」問題時，究竟是誰在解決？solve problems 呼應哲學問題；create、cause 會使哲學問題失去趣味；avoid 與 making decisions 矛盾。
章魚向燈泡噴水以「關掉」水箱燈光，且 apparently for fun；turn off the lights 為固定搭配；break into（闖入）與 bulbs 不搭。
Inky 溜出水箱、爬過地板、順排水管回到大海——著名「越獄」事件；escaping 呼應 slipped out...escaped；hunting、copying 與事件細節不符。
這種智力「引發」了嚴肅的倫理問題；raises a question 為固定搭配；settles、answers 與 keep philosophers busy、需要特別許可等展開矛盾。
「被圈養」的動物感到無聊時表現為應激：噴墨、斷腕、拒食；captive 呼應 zoos、tanks 的語境；wild、social 與水族館的場景不符。
水族館重新設計水箱使其更「有刺激、不無聊」；stimulating 與解決 boredom 的問題呼應；crowded、artificial 會加重壓力；expensive 無關。
演化「無法」同時支付發達大腦與漫長童年的資源成本；unable to spend...at the same time 呼應短壽命的事實；willing、eager 與 melancholy note 矛盾。
章魚必須獨自「掌握」幾乎一切，呼應 without parents or teachers；forget、question 與 building its brilliant mind 矛盾；teach 主語應是人。
from scratch 為固定短語「從零開始」，呼應 must master nearly everything alone；from memory（憑記憶）與無師自通矛盾。
無師自通的成就使其更加「令人敬佩」，more impressive, not less 為讓步強調；ordinary、obvious 削弱論證，useful 偏離智力主題。
獨立心智的標誌不是知道多少，而是「無人指導時能應付多少」；independent 呼應 without ever being told；obedient、artificial 與自主性矛盾。
